Emergency Evacuation at Jeep Plant, Production Completely Halted
9 photos
Photo: Stellantis North America | Facebook
The Toledo Assembly Complex plant was evacuated, and production was completely halted following a hazardous chemical release at a nearby transport facility. The spill began on Tuesday evening and led to consecutive shift cancellations and multi-mile safety orders.
The hazardous material leak originated at MC Tank Transport, a bulk liquid chemical storage and transport facility, located approximately one mile away from the Stellantis Toledo Assembly Complex North Plant.
Because the North Plant sits directly on the outer edge of the initial mandatory one-mile evacuation radius, the chemical vapor plume forced Stellantis to immediately shut down and evacuate the assembly facility for safety.
The Toledo Assembly Complex is divided into two main facilities that build Jeep's two most important models. The Jeep Wrangler, in both two- and four-door versions, rolls off the production line of the North Plant. In the meantime, the Jeep Gladiator is built at the South Plant.
In response to the incident, the Toledo Fire and Rescue Department and the Lucas County Emergency Management Agency established two safety perimeters. The one-mile radius was the immediate mandatory evacuation zone originally enforced. A strict shelter-in-place order was issued by the Toledo city government for everyone within three miles of the terminal.
The activity of the facility’s north plant was heavily disrupted. On Tuesday night, October 20, workers on the late shift were immediately sent home as the evacuation order expanded. Stellantis officially canceled both the first and second shifts for Wednesday, October 21.
The South Plant, which produces the Gladiator , was already down and not running during this week, due to an unrelated, planned production pause by Stellantis to align vehicle inventory with market demand.
The United Auto Workers Vice President, Kevin Gotinsky, explained that the union representatives are monitoring the situation to make sure Stellantis puts employees' safety first before permitting them to return to the workspace, as reported by the Detroit Free Press.
The chemical leak paralyzed not only production at the Jeep facility, but also regional transit. All train traffic was stopped along a major North Toledo rail corridor. The shutdown blocked vital freight routes used by major rail lines.
The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency and MC Tank Transport confirmed that the chemical released from the 5,500-gallon tank is glycidyl methacrylate (GMA), a highly flammable industrial liquid, used primarily to manufacture plastics, heavy-duty paints, and specialized coatings.
In the meantime, the strict shelter-in-place advisory that affected roughly 50,000 residents within a three-mile radius has been removed. However, activity at the Toledo Assembly Complex North Plant has not yet resumed. While the general evacuation zone is scaled back, the Jeep Wrangler production lines remain halted.
The risk of an explosion dropped, but the compromised tank at MC Tank Transport was left to vent its remaining gases completely. EPA is still conducting air quality testing around the industrial sector. Stellantis will greenlight production at its facility when the air quality in the area is 100% safe.
